a: Põhja-Tallinn, northwest of the old town, on Tallinn Bay
w: Fishermen and boat wrights worked this stretch of Tallinn Bay since the 14th century, giving the district its name -- Fish House. The 1870 rail line to Saint Petersburg brought factories and workers, housed in wooden cottages that still make Kalamaja the best-preserved wooden quarter in Estonia.
s: Tallinn's best-preserved wooden quarter, once a fishing hub
_facts: Estonian for 'Fish House'; traditionally a fishing district since the 14th century
One of the best-preserved wooden architecture areas in Tallinn and Estonia, built to house factory workers after the 1870 rail link to Saint Petersburg
The Tallinn railway station (Balti jaam) was built between Kalamaja and the city centre
A former railway embankment was converted in 2011 into the Culture Kilometre walking trail, passing the Creative Hub and historic Patarei Prison and Sea Fortress

w: Named for the Swedish king who commissioned the first version in 1670 -- for Tallinn's Estonian and Finnish congregations, not the Baltic Germans -- this Romanesque Revival church replaced a wooden predecessor burned in the Great Northern War. It still rings the original bells, cast in Stockholm in 1696.
_facts: Lutheran church built 1862-1870 to plans by Otto Pius Hippius; Tallinn's grandest 19th-century church
First wooden church on the site commissioned in 1670 by Swedish King Charles XI for the Estonian and Finnish population; burned down in 1710 during the Great Northern War
Romanesque Revival hall church design, ceiling held aloft without pillars
Apse fresco by Johann Köler, the first fresco in Estonia by an ethnic Estonian; still houses the original bells, cast in Stockholm in 1696

w: Built by Vickers-Armstrongs in Barrow-in-Furness and launched in 1936, this mine-laying submarine served both the Estonian Navy and, after annexation, the Soviet Navy. Until hauled out in 2011, Lembit held the record as the world's oldest submarine still afloat.
s: Once the world's oldest floating submarine, now a museum ship
_facts: One of two Kalev-class mine-laying submarines built for Estonia before World War II; now a museum ship in Tallinn
Launched 1936 at Vickers-Armstrongs, Barrow-in-Furness; served in both the Estonian Navy and the Soviet Navy
Until hauled out on 21 May 2011, was the oldest submarine still afloat in the world
Sister ship Kalev was sunk in October 1941; both named for Lembitu, an Estonian ruler who resisted the Livonian Crusades

w: Robert Gödicke's historicist palace went up in 1872 on the site of an older summer manor, and now houses the Estonian History Museum. Its park holds a stranger collection: Soviet-era statues pulled from squares across the city after the 1988 Sovereignty Declaration.
s: Historicist palace with exiled Soviet statues in its grounds
_facts: Built on the site of the earlier Maarjamäe summer manor; designed by architect Robert Gödicke, built 1872 (or 1874) in historicist style
Today used by the Estonian History Museum
The park holds an exhibition of Soviet-era statues removed from other public spaces after the 1988 Estonian Sovereignty Declaration
